page: Microsoft Azure NV12s_v2 is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine in the NVSv2 series built on the Microsoft Hyper-V platform. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel processor providing 12 dedicated vCPUs along with 224.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a substantial 18.67 GB of RAM per vCPU core. Acceleration is delivered by two NVIDIA M60 GPUs that offer a combined 16 GB of video memory for graphics-intensive and visualization processing.

Storage configuration includes 1583 GB of local solid-state drive capacity, paired with support for Azure Premium Storage. The instance does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring standard cloud networking configurations for external access. From a cost efficiency perspective, pairing legacy NVIDIA M60 accelerators with an expansive 224 GB RAM footprint offers high resource density for workloads demanding high host memory alongside moderate GPU compute, though compute efficiency for modern deep learning architectures is constrained compared to newer tensor-core architectures.

This hardware balance positions the NV12s_v2 primarily for virtual desktop infrastructure, remote graphical workstations, 3D visualization, simulation post-processing, and video encoding workflows where large working datasets must reside concurrently in host memory alongside dedicated graphic processing units.
description: Microsoft Azure NV12s_v2 is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine tailored for graphics-focused and memory-intensive enterprise tasks. Driven by an x86_64 Intel processor managed under Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 12 dedicated vCPUs and 224.0 GB of RAM, providing a generous 18.67 GB of memory per core. Compute and graphic acceleration are backed by two NVIDIA M60 GPUs featuring a total of 16 GB of VRAM. For persistent and cache storage, the instance comes equipped with 1583 GB of local SSD capacity and supports Azure Premium Storage. It operates without complimentary public IPv4 addressing. The combination of twin GPUs and an unusually high memory footprint makes the NV12s_v2 particularly well suited for remote visualization, CAD modeling, graphics-intensive virtual desktop infrastructure, simulation rendering, and memory-heavy engineering applications.
